 ::Judgment:

:
This petition is filed by the Petitioner against Respondent No.1 & 2 under Sec.166 of M.V.Act 1989 for the relief of compensation.

2. The brief facts of the case is as under; That on 06.04.2019 at about 9.30 a.m. he had been riding a motor cycle bearing Reg. No.KA-43-A-5958 on Doddaballapura - Lingaveeranahalli Road, SCCH-5 Lingaveeranahalli Cross, at that time, a driver of the car bearing Reg. No.KA-03-MF-9782 came in rash and negligent manner and dashed against him, consequent to which, petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries all over the body.

Immediately after the accident, he was shifted to Columbia Clinic, wherein he took treatment as inpatient and spent more than Rs.4,00,000/-
towards medicines, conveyance, nourishment and other incidental charges etc.,
3.

At the time of the accident, he was aged about 29 years, hale and healthy, doing agriculture work,
thereby earning Rs.30,000/- p.m. Due to accidental injuries caused to him are permanent in nature,
he cannot do his normal activities, which resulted in loss of earnings and earning capacity.
Out of this accident crime No.9/2019 is registered against the driver of the said SCCH-5 offending car before the Hosahalli Police for the offences punishable under Sec.279, 338 of IPC.
Respondent No.1 is the earlier owner, who sold the said offending car to respondent No.2, they are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation.
Hence, prays to allow the petition and grant compensation of Rs.12,00,000/- with interest.
4. On service of notice, respondent No.1/being the earlier owner of the offending car has remained absent, hence placed exparte.
Respondent No.2 has appeared and filed written statement and denied averments of the petition.
Further denied occurrence of the accident, injuries sustained by the petitioner, age, occupation and income of the petitioner, medical expenses incurred by the petitioner.

Further submitted that, respondent No.1 is the R.C.Owner of the car bearing Reg.
No.KA-03-MF-9782, who is liable to pay SCCH-5 compensation to the petitioner under all heads.

Accordingly prays to dismiss the petition.
5.

On going through the rival pleadings of the parties, this court has framed the following:
::ISSUES::
1. Whether Petitioner proves that, he has sustained grievous injuries in the motor vehicle accident that occurred on 06.04.2019 at about 9.30 a.m. near Doddaballapura - Lingaveeranahalli Road, Lingaveeranahalli Cross due to rash and negligent driving of Car bearing Reg. No.KA-03-MF-9782 dashed against the petitioner motor cycle and caused accident, as mentioned in claim petition?
Narasimhamurthy vs Kirankumar Dhanraj on 8 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/106799992/
2 2.
Whether the Petitioner is entitled for compensation?
If so how much and from whom?
3. What order or award?
6. In order to prove his case, Petitioner himself deposed his evidence as PW-1 and marked 9 documents SCCH-5 as per Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.9 and closed his evidence.
On the other hand, there is no evidence of respondents.

7. Heard the arguments and perused the evidence available on record, then my findings on the above issues are as follows:
 Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative  Issue No.2 : Partly in the Affirmative  Issue No.3 : As per final order for the  following:
 ::REASONS::
8. Issue No.1:-
In order to prove his case, petitioner has deposed his evidence as PW-1, in his chief- examination petitioner has reiterated the facts narrated in his petition.
Hence in order to avoid repetition of facts averments made in the evidence affidavit are not reiterated here.

In this regard copy of FIR is marked as Ex.P.1, copy of complaint is marked as Ex.P.2, copy of SCCH-5 charge sheet is marked as Ex.P.3, copy of mahazar is marked as Ex.P.4, copy of IMV Report is marked as Ex.P.6.
9.

On perusal of evidence of PW-1 and records those have marked i.e., FIR, complaint, charge sheet,
mahazar and IMV Report corroborates the case of the petitioner about causing of the accident dated 06.04.2019 as alleged in the petition and in the evidence of PW-1.
10.

Per contra, except filing of written statement, respondent No.2 has not taken any endeavors to disprove the petitioner's case about non-causing of the accident as alleged in the petition and evidence of PW-1.

Since in the absence of iota of evidence, I have no hesitation to believe the case of the petitioner about causing of the injuries to the petitioner out of the accident held on 06.04.2019 at SCCH-5 about 9.30 a.m. at Lingaveeranahalli Cross on Doddaballapura Lingaveeranahalli Road.
In the absence of iota of evidence, the arguments advanced by the petitioner's counsel are support the case of the petitioner.
11. The police papers speaks that, very accident is occurred due to negligence of the driver of the car bearing Reg. No.KA-03-MF-9782.

Under such circumstances, considering the said evidence and believing the evidence of the petitioner, this tribunal comes to the conclusion that, petitioner has proved the above issue No.1 in his favour.
Accordingly I have answered above Issue No.1 in the affirmative.

sentences.text: Issue No.2:-

As per the case of the petitioner, he was aged about 29 years, to prove his age,
petitioner has produced copy of aadhar card marked as Ex.P.7, wherein his date of birth is mentioned as 07.06.1985, the alleged SCCH-5 accident was occurred on 06.04.2019, accordingly relying on Ex.P.7, age of the petitioner is considered as 34 years as on the date of the accident.
Further petitioner was working as agriculturist, thereby earning Rs.30,000/- p.m.

In this regard,
petitioner has not produced any income proof documents.

13. As per the evidence of the petitioner, he had sustained Type I compound segmental fracture shaft of left humerus, intercondylar fracture of left distal humerus, radial nerve injury along with lacerations, abrasions, for the said injuries, he had undergone surgery i.e., wound debridement,
open reduction and internal fixation.

To prove the same, petitioner has exhibited copy of wound certificate marked as Ex.P.5, discharge summary marked as Ex.P.8 issued by Columbia Clinic,
wherein he took treatment as inpatient SCCH-5 from 0.04.2019 to 09.04.2019 and medical bills amounting to Rs.1,89,494/- marked as Ex.P.9.
14.
Petitioner has not examined the Doctor who has treated him nor produced the disability certificate towards the injuries sustained by him in the alleged accident.

but on perusal of the facts,
wound certificate and evidence of PW-1 corroborated to believe the injuries sustained by the petitioner out of the accident.
Accordingly petitioner is entitled for global compensation of Rs.50,000/- along with medical bills of Rs.1,89,494/- and Rs.20,000/- for pain and suffering.
Further the documents those exhibited by the petitioner indicates to the court about causing of accident to the petitioner and the sufferings out of the accidental injuries.

15. Accordingly I hold that, the Petitioner is entitled for global compensation of Rs.2,59,494/- with SCCH-5 interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization of entire amount.

16. In the case on hand, respondent No.1 being the R.C.Owner of the car bearing Reg.
No.KA-03-MF-9782 and respondent No.2 is driver of the offending vehicle.
Hence respondent No.1 is directed to deposit the award amount with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. within 60 days from the date of this order.
With these views, I have answered Issue No.2 partly in the affirmative.
17. Issue No.3:

For the reasons assigned to Issues No.1 and 2, I proceed to pass the following:
::ORDER::
The petition filed by the Petitioner under Sec.166 of the M.V. Act, 1989 is partly allowed with cost.

The Petitioner is entitled for global compensation of Rs.2,59,494/-
(Rupees Two Lakhs Fifty Nine Thousand Four Hundred Ninety Four Only) with SCCH-5 interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization.
The Respondent No.1 shall deposit award amount with interest within 60 days from the date of this order.

The Petitioner is entitled to get release 60% of the award amount through e-payment directly to his account on furnishing the Bank A/c details along with address proof and remaining 40% shall be kept in Fixed Deposit in any of the Scheduled Bank for a period of three years, in his name.
The Advocate Fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.
